title: C396 — Right-hand rear speaker connector
introduction:
I start with the right-hand rear speaker identity, then let the Function column explain the connections: its populated rows describe the woofer’s positive and negative circuits. The drawing and table work together like a map and street directory—find the cavity label in the illustration, then read its matching row rather than judging a connection by shape alone.

After identifying the circuit row, use the pigtail tables for service-part reference. This page does not establish physical viewing direction, connector access, probing, electrical test conditions or replacement methods. Size and Used remain undefined codes, and the Gauge convention is unspecified; keep those fields as reference data rather than treating them as equipment or wire-selection instructions.

edits.why: The housing projection is on the left of the displayed drawing, beside the vertical cavity labels. I use that outline only as a visual landmark. Outlined circles correspond to populated circuit rows, and gray-filled circles correspond to unassigned rows; the illustration does not identify the projection as a latch or show a release movement.

Use Cavity to connect the drawing with a row, then read across for circuit identity, color code, gauge, function and terminal identification. The positive and negative signs distinguish the woofer connections; a negative speaker designation does not establish chassis grounding. Rows without circuit assignments are unassigned positions in this reference, not a diagnosis of missing wiring.

edits.text: Identify the speaker pigtail service parts
edits.why: I compare Engineering Shell with Hard Shell in the component identity table to connect the listings. Service Part identifies the pigtail listing, while Terminal Part Number in the assignment table identifies the terminal for a populated cavity. Keep each Gauge entry with its own table because the pigtail listing and circuit rows describe different items.

Product Id supplies the European pigtail lookup associated with this connector. Its separate regional heading keeps it distinct from the Service Part and Engineering Shell identifiers in the preceding table.
